tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a real hosted backend (a REST API with a persistent database) in one call, with no account or API key. Use it when the user needs to store data, persist an app or prototype, or give a frontend a live API. Returns a manage key, a read-only public key, a starter "products" collection, the base

tools.name: list_collections
tools.description: List the collections in the project.

tools.name: create_collection
tools.description: Create a collection: a new resource (like a table) with its own REST endpoint at /api/collections/{slug}/records. Use one per kind of thing the app stores (tasks, users, orders). Free projects allow 3.

tools.name: list_records
tools.description: Read the records stored in a collection (paginated).

tools.name: create_record
tools.description: Save a record (a JSON object) in a collection so it persists. Pass the fields as data; the API returns it with an id.

tools.name: patch_record
tools.description: Merge the given fields into a record and keep the rest, e.g. {"done": true} to tick off a task. Use this for most edits.

tools.name: create_app_user
tools.description: Add an end user to the project (for apps where each user sees only their own records). No email is sent. Then call create_app_user_session to act as that user.

tools.name: create_app_user_session
tools.description: Get a 6-hour session token for an app user without email. Send it as Authorization: Bearer <session_token> to https://reqres.in/app/collections/{collection}/records, where the user only sees their own records. Real users sign in with an emailed code via /api/app-users/login.

tools.name: list_logs
tools.description: See recent requests to the project (method, path, status, timing), newest first. Use it to debug why an app's calls fail.

tools.name: update_record
tools.description: Replace all of a record's fields: fields you leave out are removed. To change some fields and keep the rest, use patch_record.

tools.name: delete_record
tools.description: Delete a record from a collection.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "create_app_user_session" references sensitive artifacts (authorization, bearer, session token). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_project, create_app_user_session · Private data: create_project, create_collection, list_records, create_record, get_record, patch_record, create_app_user, create_app_user_session, update_record, delete_record · Public sink: create_app_user, create_app_user_session · Destructive: delete_record.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_project, create_app_user_session · Private data: create_project, create_collection, list_records, create_record, get_record, patch_record, create_app_user, create_app_user_session, update_record, delete_record · Public sink: create_app_user, create_app_user_session · Destructive: delete_record

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "update_record" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Replace a record's fields." → after: "Replace all of a record's fields: fields you leave out are removed. To change some fields and keep the rest, use patch_record."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
